title: Cosh launches as a single-binary terminal coding agent
friendlyTitle: A new coding agent runs from one small program
summary: Cosh is a new open-source, Rust-based coding agent distributed as a single binary for Linux, macOS and Windows. Its first releases include a terminal interface, background subagents, model-provider configuration and an optional hosted gateway.
friendlySummary: Cosh is an open-source coding assistant for the terminal. It comes as one compiled program and can connect to different AI model providers.
whyItMatters: A self-contained binary lowers installation friction and makes local, terminal-native agent workflows easier to try. As with any young coding agent, users should review permissions, provider settings and generated changes before trusting it with important repositories.
friendlyWhyItMatters: It may be easier to install than tools with many software dependencies. Because it is new, users should still check its access and review every important change.
